subject: Human Evolution
title: Social Grooming Theory
description: A 60-second lesson on Social Grooming Theory.

hook.text: Dunbar calculated that in groups of 150, manual grooming would eat five hours a day. Nobody has that time.

buildup.text: Grooming bonds pairs. But language can bond an entire circle of listeners simultaneously.

discovery.text: Dunbar's theory: language evolved as a more efficient form of social grooming for larger groups.

twist.text: If true, language wasn't born for planning hunts or sharing facts—it was born for gossip.

climax.text: Studies confirm most human talk is still social chatter, not information exchange—sixty-five percent.

punchline.text: Language was invented for talking about people.

quiz.question: What does Dunbar's social grooming theory propose?
options: Language replaced physical grooming for bonding larger groups
Grooming is more important than language
